notes: Thresholds are product choices (when an action is worth surfacing), not tax law. The year-end checklist deadlines are statutory: Dec 31 for 401(k) deferrals, Roth conversions, RMDs and loss harvesting; the April tax-filing deadline for prior-year IRA/HSA contributions.

items.title: Check your 401(k) deferrals against this year's limit
items.detail: Payroll deferrals must post by Dec 31. Compare year-to-date deferrals with the limit in Plan > Savings and adjust your per-paycheck percentage now.

items.title: Review tax-loss harvesting before Dec 31
items.detail: Losses only count for this tax year if the sale settles by Dec 31; watch the 30-day wash-sale window across all your accounts.

items.title: Roth conversions must be completed by Dec 31
items.detail: A conversion counts for the year it is done, and recharacterization is no longer allowed. Fill the low brackets shown in the Roth planner before year end.

items.title: Take your required minimum distribution by Dec 31
items.detail: Missing an RMD triggers an excise tax. A qualified charitable distribution can satisfy part of it tax-free.

items.title: Use or fund health accounts
items.detail: FSA balances may expire at year end; HSA contributions for this year can be made until the filing deadline.
